title: Pushing the Performance Envelope of DNN-based Recommendation Systems Inference on GPUs
problem: The embedding stage is the primary bottleneck in GPU-based DLRM inference, exhibiting up to 3.2x performance slowdown and exhibiting low occupancy in standard embedding kernels. Long memory latency stalls continue to limit performance even after occupancy optimization.
motivation: As model and dataset sizes grow, optimizing GPU inference serving for DLRMs is critical to reduce inference costs while meeting acceptable latency requirements for production deployments.
method: Microarchitecture characterization identifies low occupancy and memory latency issues in embedding kernels. Compiler optimizations achieve optimal occupancy, followed by specialized software prefetching and L2 pinning techniques that complement each other to hide and reduce memory latencies.
key_novelty: Combining plug-and-play software prefetching and L2 pinning techniques as complementary methods to systematically hide and reduce memory latency in GPU embedding kernels.
contributions: Detailed microarchitecture characterization revealing low occupancy as primary bottleneck in embedding kernels
Compiler optimizations achieving 53% performance improvement through optimal kernel occupancy
Software prefetching techniques to hide memory latencies in embedding operations
L2 pinning techniques to decrease memory latencies, achieving up to 103% embedding stage speedup

metrics.speedup: 103% for embedding stage, 77% for overall DLRM inference pipeline

limitations: Evaluation limited to AI00 GPUs with large models and datasets; generalization to other GPU architectures, older GPU generations, or memory-constrained deployments is not discussed.
primary_theme: Memory optimization for GPU recommendation system inference
